name: Amazon Keyspaces
tagline: Serverless, CQL-compatible Cassandra service on AWS with no clusters to manage.
description: Amazon Keyspaces lets you point existing Cassandra drivers and CQL at a serverless AWS endpoint instead of running a ring yourself. Under the hood it is not Cassandra but AWS's own storage layer, so there is no compaction, repair or node sizing; capacity is on-demand or provisioned, and data is replicated across three AZs with optional multi-region replication. It is a pragmatic landing zone for Cassandra workloads moving to AWS, but compatibility is partial: some CQL features, consistency levels and system tables differ, so test before you migrate.

pricing.notes: On-demand per read/write request unit or provisioned capacity, plus storage. Limited first-year free tier.

scale.notes: Automatic partition scaling; multi-Region replication with last-writer-wins conflict resolution.

strengths: No Cassandra operations: no repair, compaction or node management
Works with standard open-source Cassandra drivers and CQL
Point-in-time recovery and encryption at rest by default
IAM authentication and integration with the AWS security model
weaknesses: Partial CQL compatibility; unsupported features include some secondary index and UDF patterns
Per-request pricing can exceed self-managed Cassandra at sustained high throughput
Lightweight transactions are billed at a premium and behave differently from Cassandra
useCases: Moving existing Cassandra apps to AWS without ops
Spiky workloads that suit on-demand pricing
Serverless apps that need a CQL data model
notIdealFor: Apps relying on full Cassandra feature parity
